headline: Your all-time favourites

videos.title: Gym edit with body-mask wipe transitions

stats.quote: From Instagram's embed page, fetched 2026-11-04: 25,163 likes · 483 comments (Instagram doesn't show the view count there)

hook.verbatim: The one thing i love about the gym… Is that it can't be faked.
hook.summary: Described by Constantin: a mix of gym footage, sound effects (SFX) and wipe transitions built on body masks, where a person walking across the frame is masked out and becomes the wipe into the next shot. The quoted line is the caption's opening.

videos.formula: Gym B-roll cut on SFX hits → each cut is a body-mask wipe (someone walks across the frame and reveals the next shot) → caption carries a short manifesto about earned physiques
videos.why: Constantin's pick. The transitions are motivated by real movement in the frame, so the edit feels physical rather than like a template effect, and SFX sell every wipe. Per the caption it was shot on a DJI Osmo Action 4 and edited in Adobe Premiere Pro, tagged #gymedit. 25K likes is modest; it's here as a craft reference, not as viral proof.

production.vfx: Body-mask wipe transitions with SFX on each wipe (per Constantin); a floating phone-screen composite is visible in the cover

videos.replicate: For a PT gym: lock off 6–10 short training shots (one angle each) and, between them, have someone walk close past the lens. In Premiere Pro (or CapCut's masking), mask the walker's body frame by frame and reveal the next clip behind them; add a whoosh or impact SFX on every wipe and cut to the beat. Action camera or phone at 50–60 fps makes the masking easier. End on the strongest rep.

remix.gym_pt: Members training, one locked-off angle per shot; a trainer walking past the lens wipes into the next member. SFX on every wipe, end on a PR.
remix.massage: Treatment-room B-roll (oil, hands, stretch); the therapist walking past the camera wipes into the next technique. Soft whoosh instead of impact hits.
remix.dexa_biohacking: Client walks past the lens and reveals them lying on the DEXA table, then the printout; a second walk-by reveals the 12-week rescan.
remix.icebath: A walk-by wipe from the sauna door to the plunge, then from the gasp to the calm exhale; ice-crack SFX on each wipe.
remix.photo_video: Showreel structure for your own work: each walk-by in an event clip wipes into the next client's best shot. Use it to show range in 20 seconds.

story.do: Gym shot cut on a hard SFX hit
A walk-by body mask reveals the next shot
Caption manifesto: “it can't be faked”

why.says: Transitions come from real movement, not templates

steps.do: Lock off 6–10 short training shots
Have someone walk close past the lens
Mask the walker and reveal the next clip
Add a whoosh or impact on every wipe

guide.avoid: Don't film members without their consent

videos.title: Partner decompression massage you can do at home

stats.quote: Reported by Constantin from the post on Instagram, 2026-11-08: 40K+ likes (Instagram's embed page doesn't show this post's count, so the exact number isn't read yet)

hook.summary: Caption: “Decompress and relax your partner’s ENTIRE body with these simple but amazing techniques at home.” The cover shows a hands-on spinal decompression on a partner lying head-down, with word-by-word subtitles (“completely relaxed,”). (From the cover and caption; the video itself wasn't watched.)

videos.formula: Promise for couples (“relax your partner’s entire body”) → hands-on techniques shown on a real partner → burned-in word-by-word subtitles → follow CTA
videos.why: Constantin's pick. It turns professional bodywork into something a viewer can try on their partner tonight, which makes it shareable between couples. The caption carries an “educational only” disclaimer.
videos.replicate: Therapist demonstrates 3 partner techniques on a real couple, one per beat, with big word-by-word subtitles; end with “send this to your partner” and a booking line. Keep the creator's “educational only” framing and don't show anything that could hurt a spine.

remix.massage: “3 moves to relax your partner tonight”: therapist coaches a real couple, subtitles word by word, end on “book the real thing”.
remix.gym_pt: “Stretch your partner after leg day”: a trainer coaches a couple through 3 assisted stretches.
remix.dexa_biohacking: “Wind your partner down for better sleep”: a 3-step evening routine coached by the clinic, framed as general wellbeing, not treatment.
remix.icebath: “Warm your partner up after the plunge”: a quick towel-and-breath routine coached by the guide.
remix.photo_video: Film a couples' session in this tutorial style: close hands, the partner's face, big subtitles.

story.do: Promise: relax your partner's entire body
Techniques shown hands-on on a real partner
Follow CTA, plus “educational only” disclaimer

why.says: Something to try on your partner tonight
Couples send it to each other

steps.do: Film a real couple who both agree
Show three simple techniques, one per beat
Burn in big word-by-word subtitles
End on “send this to your partner”

guide.avoid: No spinal pressure claims or risky moves

videos.title: “Don't spill the water” challenge at a local gym

stats.quote: From Instagram's embed page, fetched 2026-11-08: 39,069 likes · 123 comments (Instagram doesn't show the view count there)

hook.summary: Big on-screen title over gym footage of members attempting the challenge; the cover shows a member drinking from a glass while holding a dumbbell, others watching. The caption adds a membership offer, address and phone number. (From the cover and caption; the video itself wasn't watched.)

videos.formula: Named challenge as the on-screen title → members attempt it in front of the group → the caption sells a membership offer with location and contact
videos.why: Constantin's pick. A local gym turned a simple party-game challenge into reach (39K likes) and paired it with a direct offer in the caption: entertainment on screen, the sale in the caption.
videos.replicate: Pick one simple, funny challenge members can attempt in 20 seconds; film 4–6 attempts from one angle with the title on screen; best fail and best win last; put the offer, address and booking line in the caption, not the video.

remix.gym_pt: Run a monthly challenge (plank-and-sip, wall-sit balance) with members; title on screen, offer in the caption.
remix.massage: “Don't spill the oil” balance challenge for therapists at a team day, or a calm “stay relaxed” challenge for clients.
remix.dexa_biohacking: “Guess your body-fat %” challenge: members guess, then the DEXA printout reveals it.
remix.icebath: “Don't flinch” challenge: hold a glass of water steady while stepping into the plunge.
remix.photo_video: Film a client's challenge day for them; deliver the edit with the title card and their offer in the caption.

story.do: Title card: “Don't spill the water challenge”
Members attempt it while the group watches
Caption sells membership with address and phone

why.says: Simple, funny challenge anyone can judge
Entertainment on screen, the sale in caption

steps.do: Pick one 20-second challenge members can try
Film 4–6 attempts from one angle
Put the challenge name on screen
Offer, address and booking line in caption

guide.avoid: Keep the challenge safe for every member

videos.title: “LOVE” trend, athlete edition: bicep heart as the O

stats.quote: From Instagram's embed page, fetched 2026-11-08: 90,467 likes · 546 comments (Instagram doesn't show the view count there)

hook.verbatim: Love trend, but make it athlete edition. 💀
hook.summary: The LOVE trend: the letters L, V and E appear around the creator while his flexed arms form a heart for the “O”. The cover shows a shirtless athlete against a wall with the letters overlaid. (From the cover and caption; the video itself wasn't watched.)

videos.formula: Join a running trend (LOVE spelled with the body) → twist it to your niche (“athlete edition”) → the physique makes the punchline
videos.why: Constantin's pick. It rides an existing trend people already recognise and adds one niche twist, so it travels with the trend's reach. 90K likes and 546 comments.
videos.replicate: Watch which body or letter trends are running this week, then shoot your niche version the same day: one locked-off shot, the letters added in edit, the trainer's or member's pose as the payoff.

remix.gym_pt: LOVE trend with a member's bicep heart, or the trainer and a client making the O together.
remix.massage: LOVE trend with the therapist's hands making the heart over a client's back.
remix.dexa_biohacking: LOVE spelled with DEXA printouts, the heart made by two hands over the body-fat number.
remix.icebath: LOVE spelled with ice cubes, the O as a heart drawn in the frost on the tub.
remix.photo_video: Do the trend with camera gear: two lenses forming the heart.

story.do: “Love trend, but make it athlete edition”
Letters L, V, E appear around him
Flexed arms form the heart as the O

why.says: Rides a trend people already recognise
One niche twist makes it his own

steps.do: Spot a body or letter trend this week
Shoot one locked-off full-body take
Add the letters in the edit
Make your niche's pose the punchline

guide.avoid: Post while the trend is still running

videos.title: Cake cut with a knife on the barbell during a bench press

stats.quote: From Instagram's embed page, fetched 2026-11-08: 57,686 likes · 643 comments (Instagram doesn't show the view count there)

hook.summary: The cover shows a lifter on the bench with a long knife fixed to the barbell, lowering it into a big cake while a crowd films on phones; Russian text on the cover reads “viral content, the tradition continues”. The caption says “40M VIEWS 😳 10K FOLLOWERS = CAKE CUT 🎂”, a promise to repeat the stunt at a follower milestone (it's unclear whether the 40M refers to this reel). (From the cover and caption; the video itself wasn't watched.)

videos.formula: Absurd stunt with gym equipment (a barbell becomes a cake knife) → crowd filming on phones → milestone promise (“10K followers = cake cut”) turns it into a recurring tradition
videos.why: Constantin's pick. One impossible-looking image explains the whole video, and the milestone promise gives followers a reason to come back. 57K likes and 643 comments on the embed page.
videos.replicate: Celebrate a gym milestone (members, followers, anniversary) with one safe, visual stunt using your own equipment; film the crowd's phones as well as the moment; promise the next one at the next milestone. Keep it safe: a spotter, a blunt prop instead of a real blade, nobody under the bar.

remix.gym_pt: Milestone stunt: the strongest member cuts the anniversary cake with a (blunt) prop on the bar; promise the next one at the next follower goal.
remix.massage: Studio birthday: the therapist “massages” the cake with a wooden tool; milestone promise in the caption.
remix.dexa_biohacking: The cake comes out of the scanner on the DEXA table for the clinic's 1,000th scan.
remix.icebath: Cut the anniversary cake with an ice block; the crowd films on their phones.
remix.photo_video: Shoot the crowd filming as much as the stunt: phones in the foreground sell the moment.

story.do: Knife fixed to a barbell over a cake
Bench press lowers the blade through the cake
Crowd films on phones, milestone promise in caption

why.says: One impossible image explains the whole video
Milestone promise makes followers come back

steps.do: Tie a stunt to a gym milestone
Use a blunt prop and a spotter
Film the crowd's phones as well as the stunt
Promise the next one at the next goal

guide.avoid: Never use a real blade near lifters

videos.title: Fake CCTV “robbery” skit for a restaurant in Biel/Bienne

hook.summary: A fake local news story: “breaking news Biel/Bienne” over an overhead CCTV-style shot, staff with their hands up as a “robber” walks in. Per the caption he gets distracted by an ad sign, makes himself a pita in the kitchen and leaves full; the CCTV reveals the real culprit, the Pita Gyros Raclette. The caption ends by saying the scene is fiction. (From the cover and caption; the video itself wasn't watched.)

videos.formula: Fake breaking-news lower third + CCTV angle → staged “robbery” at the counter → the robber gets distracted by the product → the product is revealed as the culprit; caption confirms it's fiction
videos.why: Constantin's pick. The city name, date and time make locals stop scrolling, the CCTV look reads as real footage, and the product is the punchline, so the ad doesn't feel like an ad. It's a business in Biel/Bienne, the same Swiss market Constantin films in.

production.vfx: Breaking-news lower third over a high, CCTV-style angle

videos.replicate: For a client: build a fake local news story around their product. Shoot from a high corner like a security camera, add a “breaking news” lower third with the city name, let staff play along, make the product the twist, and say clearly in the caption that it's fiction. Agree the framing with the business first and keep it obviously playful, so nobody mistakes it for a real crime report.

remix.gym_pt: “Break-in at the gym”: CCTV shows a ‘burglar’ who stops to train on the new rack; the real culprit is the PT offer.
remix.massage: A CCTV ‘intruder’ sneaks into the studio, gets distracted by the treatment table and leaves relaxed; the culprit is the 60-minute deep tissue.
remix.dexa_biohacking: Breaking news: a suspect caught on CCTV stepping into the DEXA scanner; the culprit is the body-composition report.
remix.icebath: An intruder comes to steal the ice and ends up in the plunge; breaking-news lower third with your city.
remix.photo_video: Sell it as a package to local businesses: a fake breaking-news CCTV skit, shot in one afternoon.

story.do: “Breaking news Biel/Bienne” over CCTV-style footage
“Robber” walks in, staff raise their hands
He gets distracted and makes himself a pita
Reveal: the pita gyros raclette is the culprit

why.says: City name and time make locals stop
Product is the punchline, so it's no ad

steps.do: Frame a fake local news story around the product
Shoot from a high corner like CCTV
Add a breaking-news lower third with the city
Make the product the twist and the culprit
Say clearly in the caption it's fiction

guide.avoid: Don't let it pass as a real crime
